title: Breaking feature collapse in self-supervised time series encoders
claim: Scaling model size yields saturating or declining accuracy for existing general-purpose encoders, while the proposed family keeps improving and sits higher.
layout: single scatter-line plot, log-x parameters vs accuracy, direct family labels, no legend
description: A single line-and-marker plot with a log-scaled x-axis, Number of Parameters [M], from about 0.3 to 400. The y-axis is Avg. Performance [%], from about 53 to 70. Light dashed grid lines run behind the data. Three model families are drawn as colored lines with round markers and labeled directly in monospace text, with no legend. UniTS in green sits at the lower left. It rises steeply from about 54 to 59.5 and then goes flat or slips slightly. MOMENT in purple runs from about 20M to 300M parameters and climbs slowly from about 67 to 68.3. OTIS in red lies above MOMENT. It starts at about 7M parameters at 67.7 and reaches 70 at about 130M. The eye goes first to the red line at the top right, then to the flat curves below it.
caption: General-purpose time series encoders saturate at scale. Average accuracy over 23 UEA and 120 UCR datasets. Across three general-purpose encoder families, gains through parameter scaling saturate. OTIS-7.1M nearly matches the 43× larger MOMENT-308M.
abstract: General-purpose time series encoders promise a single backbone that generalises across tasks and domains; however, they currently do not scale. We trace this down to a critical point of failure: under the predominant masked data modelling supervision, the encoder's output tokens partially collapse. This is the natural consequence of supervising encoders only in the input space, which leaves no constraint against redundant token dimensions in the feature space. We introduce OTISv2, which suppresses the collapse by complementing the reconstruction objective in input space with two objectives in the feature space: a self-distillation loss against an exponential-moving-average teacher, and a KoLeo regulariser. Under matched training, the resulting encoder reduces the cosine similarity and lifts the effective rank of its output tokens relative to its predecessor, and it scales monotonically from 7.1 M to 116 M parameters where its predecessor declines. It matches or surpasses existing general-purpose time series encoders across 143 uni- and multi-variate datasets. To foster further research, we release our code and pre-trained weights.
